verdicts.strongest_argument: Every element of this finding is in the one corpus document the hunter cited, and it is aggregator copy, not an obscure filing footnote. docs/5a3f3cc3c258ffdf842ca4dcebc73e57b6d02171.txt carries a #INSIDERS digest on 2026-07-10 naming 'Globalharvest bought 1,179,087 shares at $13.00-$13.50 worth approximately $15.8 mln', a second on 2026-07-13 naming the 592,957-share/$7.9m tranche, a filingtracker link to accession 0000899140-26-000708 posted 2026-07-09T20:24:29Z (nine minutes after acceptance), a merlintrader 'biggest insider buys Jul 6-10' roundup on 2026-07-11, and a 2026-07-10T13:25:25Z post that independently states the two interpretive points the finding leans on -- the odd item-8.01 8-K 'only one month after buyback authorization' and 'almost 45% tightly held'. The magnitude and the read were both published. The bars then confirm the market saw it: AVO went 12.49 (07-02) to 13.29 (07-06) to 13.50 (07-08), +8.1% over four sessions on 1.8-2.1m shares against a 518k 20d average -- 3.5x volume on the exact accumulation days -- and faded back to 12.6-12.9 through late July on 500-800k. That is the information arriving, being priced, and being sold into. The claim's own logic ('if it were priced AVO would not trade below the buyer's range') is the error: a stock can price an informed buy and still drift with avocado pricing and the Q3 EBITDA guide of $28-32m that was published 2026-06-08. Finally the mechanism is thin against this print: Form 4s from early July say nothing about the July-quarter P&L, and the buyback progress the 8-K disclosed is a use of the authorisation the company announced 2026-06-03, already in the corpus.

prior_publication.what_it_says: '$15.81 million purchase by 10% owner' with a direct link to the 13D/A accession, posted nine minutes after EDGAR acceptance.
AVO appears in a syndicated 'twenty biggest insider buys and sells, Jul 6-10' roundup.
Smartinsider ranked AVO positive on insider activity on 2026-06-16, before the July tranche.
The $100m buyback authorised 2026-06-03 and the $25m Calavo synergy target were both public in the same digest, with 'recent insider buying of ~220,000 shares' already flagged.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: quote.json: +8.1% from the 2026-07-02 close of 12.49 to the 2026-07-08 close of 13.50 on 1.78-2.07m shares/day versus a 517,575 20d average, i.e. the accumulation window is the single highest-volume non-earnings stretch in the file. Subsequent fade to 12.52-12.87 on 350-770k. Baseline run_up_20d_pct is -2.13% and spot 12.87, so the buyer's range has been fully given back -- but that fade happened on light volume with the July Form 4s already public.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: Evidence that Globalharvest bought again inside the blackout or after 2026-08-01 at prices near 12.5-13.0, which would be an unpublished datapoint rather than a re-reading of July filings the aggregators already carried.

interactions: The finding and its own 'independence' paragraph rest on the same document (docs/5a3f3cc3c258ffdf842ca4dcebc73e57b6d02171.txt) for every dollar figure, as the hunter concedes; that document is also the thing that establishes prior publication, so the corroboration cannot raise the novelty.
corpus_limits: The 13D/A and 8-K item-8.01 bodies are not stored in docs/, so the exact affiliate ownership percentage and the buyback share count are only available at aggregator precision. No news channel items exist for AVO in any sweep, which is a capture artefact and not evidence that wire coverage was absent. No option chain, so no implied move to test the claim against. No tripwire-flagged documents were excluded.
